plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Purple-blue spikes ripple across the sun-baked plateaus of Provence in long, fragrant rows. The air hums with bees and smells sweetly herbal. Late June is when the true lavender fields reach their dramatic peak.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, with true lavender peaking from late June to mid-July
plants.location: Provence, southern France (including the Valensole Plateau)
plants.funFact: The name lavender is thought to come from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Dinner-plate-sized pink blooms rise above the still water on tall stalks, held clear of the round, water-beading leaves. Each flower opens in the morning and closes at night. Summer is lotus season in the ponds and moats of East Asia.
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across East Asia, including Japan and China
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic texture that sheds water and dirt. This 'lotus effect' has inspired self-cleaning paints and fabrics.

plants.name: Banksia menziesii
plants.description: In the Australian winter, this gnarled, sandy-soil tree lights up with woolly flower spikes in shades of red, pink and gold. They look like candles and are a feast for honeyeaters when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to winter, with peak flowering from May to July
plants.location: Southwest Western Australia, on sandy coastal plains
plants.funFact: Each flower spike is made up of hundreds of tiny individual flowers. Banksias are adapted to bushfire, and many species release their seeds after a fire.
